$comment: UX-P117 / #2060 item 1 — THE SIX CHIPS ONE TAP AFTER 'BAD', AND WHERE EACH ROUTES.
Ruling 021: when several consumers must agree about the same input, the unit to
share is the DECISION, not the ingredient. Three runtimes render this chip row —
Python declares the vocabulary and the routes, Swift draws the chips on the
native surface, TypeScript draws them on /admin/labeling — and no import spans
them. So the shared unit is this table.
WHY IT MATTERS. The chips exist to turn a Bad into ROUTABLE DEFECT EVIDENCE.
Measured on production 2026-08-21: 88 ranking_judgments, ZERO carrying
`label_metadata.fixable_interest`, and 71 of them bad/kill WITH reason tags. The
cluster endpoints skip any row without that key, so both had returned an empty
list for the life of the store while Alex had flagged `stale` 35 separate times.
The label was recorded and the complaint was dropped, every time.
THE PART THAT IS EASY TO GET WRONG IS `tag`, NOT `display`. The stored tag is
the STORE's canonical spelling, so 'Confusing' stores `unclear` and 'Boring'
stores `low_stakes` — the corpus already holds 16 and 6 rows under those names.
A surface that shipped `confusing` as a new tag would split the tally the chips
exist to grow, which is exactly what had already happened: /admin/labeling wrote
`boring` (2 rows) beside native's `low_stakes` (6 rows), one complaint counted
twice, each half too small to look like anything. Canonicalisation lives in
app/utils/discover_reason_tags.py and nowhere else.
`fix_type` values are NOT new. They are the vocabulary the web ReviewTab's
FIX_TYPES select already offers and the cluster endpoints already group by, so a
native chip tap lands in the SAME cluster as a web triage of the same problem.
ORDER IS THE TAP ORDER, by measured frequency of the complaint each names, so
the most common answer is the shortest reach on a phone. `stale` leads because
it is 40% of the corpus.

$notification_comment: #2060 item 6 — the labelling nudge rides the EXISTING morning digest as a
notification ACTION rather than as a second push (notifications v1 is
It is an action and not the tap target because a push has ONE tap target and
the digest's is the most interesting market of the day. Overwriting it would
take the market away from the one person who most wants it. The client
registers the category unconditionally; the SERVER attaches it only for an
admin recipient, because the digest renders one payload and broadcasts it —
an unconditional line would tell the whole user base to go and label.
